rounds.text: Uniparts India Ltd trades at a modest P/E of 22 [E1], which sits below the sector benchmark P/E of 26.88x [E6], offering an attractive entry point given the company's superior financial returns. Specifically, the company delivers an impressive ROCE of 21.06% against a sector benchmark of 12.54% [E10], alongside a robust ROE of 18.19% beating the sector's 11.39% [E9], demonstrating highly efficient capital allocation. Operational momentum is exceptionally strong, marked by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 27% [E16], an 88% surge in trailing profit growth [E19], and an expanding operating margin reaching 24% in June 2026 compared to 19% in the prior-year quarter [E26]. Furthermore, cash generation is pristine with an operating cash flow of Rs 174 Cr in March 2026 [E30] and a cash conversion ratio of 1.10x ensuring profits are fully backed by cash [E29], all while maintaining a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.18x [E33]. Conceded: the company has experienced poor historical sales growth of 5.32% over the past five years [E56] and a 3-year compounded sales decline of -5% [E15]. Management visibility remains highly constructive, backed by a robust trailing twelve-month new business order book of over INR 225 crores [E83] and expectations that full-year FY27 revenue growth will exceed FY26 levels by a couple of percentage points [E71].

Conceded: the company demonstrates healthy short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 3.76x [E34] and strong TTM revenue growth of 27% [E16]. However, longer-term historical performance reveals persistent top-line fragility, with compounded sales growth over 3 years sitting at -5% [E15] and over 5 years lagging at just 5% [E14], alongside a poor 5-year sales growth rate flagged by filed statements [E56]. Furthermore, profit growth has proved similarly erratic, showing a 3-year compounded contraction of -8% [E18] and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend over the last 3 years [E27]. Valuation metrics also stretch well beyond sector norms, with the price-to-book ratio at 4.66x against a sector benchmark of 2.8x [E7] and the EV/EBITDA multiple at 14.25x compared to a sector benchmark of 12.62x [E11]. These high multiples rest on fragile ground as domestic institutional investors have aggressively reduced their holdings by 6.10 percentage points from Sep 2023 to Jun 2026 [E39]. Finally, external vulnerabilities weigh heavily on operations, with management explicitly noting that ongoing West Asia tensions exert pressure on input costs and supply chains [E89], while tariff-driven price volatility and macroeconomic uncertainty continue to spur demand deferrals and customer purchasing moderation [E90, E91].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is -5% [E15] and 3-year compounded profit growth is -8% [E18]. However, focusing on historical contractions ignores the explosive inflection in recent performance, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 27% [E16] and profit growth of 88% [E19]. The bear's concern over valuation multiples ignores Uniparts' superior return profile, featuring a robust ROCE of 21.06% [E10] and ROE of 18.19% [E9] that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks of 12.54% and 11.39%. Regarding institutional holding changes [E39], overall institutional money flow actually reads POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with a net positive holding change [E40], and the business maintains an exceptionally conservative balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.18x [E33]. Finally, while external pressures exist [E89, E90], management reports robust demand in construction equipment supported by U.S. and European infrastructure spending [E74], alongside a strong trailing twelve-month new business order book exceeding INR 225 crores [E83].

Conceded: Trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 27% [E16] and profit growth hit 88% [E19]. However, this recent acceleration rests on an inconsistent margin trend over the last three years [E27] and one quarter [E28], driven by a product mix shift rather than structural stability [E81]. The bull cites superior ROCE of 21.06% [E10] and ROE of 18.19% [E9], but ignores that this valuation demands a price-to-book ratio of 4.66x against a sector benchmark of just 2.8x [E7], alongside a higher EV/EBITDA of 14.25x compared to the sector's 12.62x [E11]. While the bull highlights positive institutional money flow [E40], domestic institutions have aggressively reduced their holdings from 11.04% in September 2023 to 4.94% in June 2026 [E39]. Conceded: The new business order book exceeds INR 225 crores [E83]. Yet borrowings climbed to Rs 155 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 120 Cr a year earlier [E35], while the business faces active headwinds from West Asian geopolitical pressures [E89], tariff-driven price volatility, and consumer purchasing deferrals in the aftermarket [E90].

The bear points to inconsistent operating margin trends [E27, E28] and product mix shifts [E81], but ignores that operating margins have actually expanded to 22% in the TTM and reached 24% in the June 2026 quarter [E25, E26]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings moved from 11.04% to 4.94% [E39], but overall institutional money flow remains registered as positive due to other inflows [E40]. While borrowings rose to Rs 155 Cr [E35], the company simultaneously maintains a substantial net cash balance of approximately INR 190 crores and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E33, E86]. Conceded: the bear highlights EV/EBITDA of 14.25x against the sector's 12.62x [E11], yet this valuation is fully justified by a superior ROCE of 21.06% and ROA of 14.38% that heavily outperform sector benchmarks of 12.54% and 6.04% [E8, E10]. Finally, external supply chain pressures [E89] have not hindered operational momentum, as evidenced by a robust TTM new business order book exceeding INR 225 crores [E83] and EBITDA surging 55% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 [E80].

Conceded: TTM operating margins reached 22% and June 2026 reached 24% [E25, E26]. However, the bull ignores that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly classified as inconsistent over the last 3 years and 1 quarter, reflecting underlying volatility in profitability [E27, E28]. While the bull dismisses the drop in domestic institutional holdings from 11.04% to 4.94% [E39] by citing general positive money flow [E40], this massive 6.10 percentage point exit by sophisticated domestic funds signals a profound lack of local confidence. The bull's focus on a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E33] overlooks the concrete reality that total borrowings increased to Rs 155 Cr from Rs 120 Cr a year earlier [E35]. Furthermore, arguing that a higher EV/EBITDA of 14.25x versus the sector benchmark of 12.62x [E11] is justified by superior returns ignores that longer-term historical sales growth over 5 years is weak at 5% and negative at -5% over 3 years [E14, E15], pointing to structural stagnation that premium multiples fail to reflect. Finally, the bull minimizes external supply chain pressures [E89], but management explicitly noted that tariff-driven price volatility and economic uncertainty continue to cause demand deferrals, purchasing moderation in the aftermarket, and tempered big-ticket equipment purchases [E90, E91].

evidence.quote: keeping that in mind and the visibility that we have, our FY27 growth will be a couple of percentage points bigger than the growth that we had in FY26 on a year-on-year basis.

evidence.fact: Q2 FY27 operational performance is expected to remain robust and in line with Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Q2 looks very robust, and I think Q2 should be in line with Q1.

evidence.fact: Mexico warehouse operations are projected to generate mid-single-digit million-dollar revenue in FY27.
evidence.quote: For FY27, we believe that this revenue should be in mid-single-digit million dollar level.

evidence.fact: Demand in construction equipment is being sustained by infrastructure spending in the U.S. and government investments in Europe.
evidence.quote: Infrastructure-led spending, particularly under the technology investments in the U.S. and the government-led investments in Europe, is sustaining healthy customer schedules and order visibility.

evidence.fact: Leading OEMs view calendar year 2026 as the cyclical bottom for large agricultural equipment, expecting recovery in calendar year 2027.
evidence.quote: Leading OEMs have indicated that current year 2026 represents the cyclical bottom with a more meaningful recovery expected through calendar year 2027.

evidence.fact: Small agricultural equipment in India is performing well, supported by government subsidy programs and increasing adoption in mid-to-higher horsepower categories.
evidence.quote: In the small agriculture equipment, India continues to perform well, supported by government subsidy programs and rising adoption across the mid-to-higher horsepower categories.

evidence.fact: Restoration of the finishing shop at the Ludhiana facility is progressing on schedule without causing customer supply disruption.
evidence.quote: On that note, the restoration of the finishing shop at our Ludhiana facility is progressing well and on schedule.

evidence.fact: First customer deliveries from the Mexico warehouse operations are expected to begin in Q3 of this fiscal year.
evidence.quote: Equally, our Mexico operations are on track with first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 of this year.

evidence.fact: Capital expenditure during Q1 FY27 was INR 12 crores, focusing on capacity enhancement, productivity, and customer-led initiatives.
evidence.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter was INR12 crores, in line with ongoing investment plans focused on capacity enhancement, productivity improvement and customer-led growth initiatives.

evidence.fact: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 reached INR 90 crores, marking a 55% year-on-year growth and 10% sequential growth.
evidence.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR90 crores, registering strong 55% growth year-on-year and 10% growth sequentially, reflecting healthy operating leverage and disciplined cost management across the business.

evidence.fact: Material cost in Q1 FY27 was 33.3%, primarily reflecting a shift in product mix.
evidence.quote: So Viraj, if you look at it, our cost of materials this time is about 33.3%, And I think it's coming at 33.3% largely because there's been a product mix change.

evidence.fact: Management maintains that material costs normally range between 34% and 37% over the business cycle.
evidence.quote: I think what we've always maintained is that our material cost should be in the range of 34% to 37%, and that's typical of our business.

evidence.fact: Trailing 12-month new business order book stands at over INR 225 crores.
evidence.quote: On the business development front, our trailing 12-month new business order book remains robust at over INR225 crores with a healthy pipeline.

evidence.fact: Construction equipment business contributed 45% of total revenue in Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Ashutosh, you are right that in Q1 FY27, the business has really seen a good growth in the construction business, which is today 45% of our total revenue.

evidence.fact: The company's trailing twelve-month new business order book stands at over INR 225 crore.
evidence.quote: On the business development front, our trailing twelve-month new business order book remains robust at over INR 225 crore, with a healthy pipeline.

evidence.fact: Net cash balance stood at approximately INR 190 crores at the end of Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Our net cash position at the end of quarter 1 stands at INR190 crores, reflecting the continued strength of our cash generation.

evidence.fact: Operating cash flow generated during Q1 FY27 was INR 44 crores.
evidence.quote: We generated INR44 crores of operating cash during the quarter, and our 12-month trailing EPS stands at INR39.97, reflecting sustained improvement in earnings over the past year.

evidence.fact: The company is actively evaluating about half a dozen acquisition opportunities.
evidence.quote: I think today, we have about half a dozen opportunities that we are closely looking at.

evidence.fact: Ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia continue to exert pressure on supply chains and input costs.
evidence.quote: The ongoing West Asia situation has continued to exert pressure on input costs and supply chains.

evidence.quote: The tariff-driven price volatility has led to some demand skewing, as higher prices caused customers and channel partners to moderate their purchasing.
